title: Why Railroads Don't Need Expansion Joints
summary: Practical Engineering explains how continuous welded rail copes with thermal expansion by restraining it, using the relationship between temperature, stress and strain. The video is part of a series on railways.
why: Linked in rail and heat-related threads as the clear explanation of why railroads need no expansion joints and how heat problems are handled.

quote.text: Practical Engineering already explained the correct solution to this problem
